SELECT 
    d.name AS Department
	,e.name AS Employee
	,max_salary AS Salary
FROM Department d JOIN (
     Employee e JOIN (
        SELECT
            departmentId
            ,max(salary) AS max_salary
        FROM Employee

) ON d.id = e.departmentId

movie-rating.code:
(
    WITH cte AS (
        SELECT
            user_id,
            COUNT(*) AS rating
        FROM MovieRating
        GROUP BY user_id
    )
    SELECT
        name AS results
    FROM cte
    LEFT JOIN Users
        ON cte.user_id = Users.user_id
    WHERE rating = (
        SELECT MAX(rating)
        FROM cte
    )
    ORDER BY name
    LIMIT 1
)

UNION ALL

(
    WITH c AS (
        SELECT
            movie_id,
            AVG(rating) AS avg
        FROM MovieRating
        WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_at) = 2020
          AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM created_at) = 2
        GROUP BY movie_id
    )
    SELECT
        title AS results
    FROM c
    LEFT JOIN Movies m
        ON c.movie_id = m.movie_id
    WHERE avg = (
        SELECT MAX(avg)
        FROM c
    )
    ORDER BY title
    LIMIT 1
);

confirmation-rate.code:
# Write your MySQL query statement below

select S.user_id, coalesce(round((Confirmed.confirmed/Total.total), 2), 0) as confirmation_rate
from Signups as S
left join (
    select user_id, count(user_id) as total
    from Confirmations as C group by user_id
) as Total
    on S.user_id = Total.user_id
left join (
    select user_id, count(action) as confirmed
    from Confirmations as C group by user_id, action having action='confirmed'
) as Confirmed
    on S.user_id = Confirmed.user_id

restaurant-growth.code:
-- d.visited_on+6 as visited_on, sum(amount) as amount, round(avg(amount), 2) as average_amount
SELECT
    d.visited_on+6 as visited_on,
    SUM(c.amount) AS amount,
    ROUND(SUM(c.amount) / 7.0, 2) AS average_amount
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT visited_on
    FROM Customer
) AS d
JOIN Customer c
    ON c.visited_on BETWEEN d.visited_on AND d.visited_on + 6
WHERE d.visited_on + 6 <= (
    SELECT MAX(visited_on)
    FROM Customer
)
GROUP BY d.visited_on
ORDER BY d.visited_on;

department-top-three-salaries.code:
-- Write your PostgreSQL query statement below

SELECT
    dept_name AS "Department",
    emp_name AS "Employee",
    salary AS "Salary"
FROM (
    SELECT
        dept_name,
        emp_name,
        salary,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY dept_name
            ORDER BY salary DESC
        ) AS salary_rank
    FROM (
        SELECT
            d.name AS dept_name,
            e.name AS emp_name,
            salary
        FROM Employee e
        LEFT JOIN Department d
            ON e.departmentId = d.id
    )
)
WHERE salary_rank <= 3;

average-time-of-process-per-machine.code:
-- Write your PostgreSQL query statement below
SELECT
    machine_id,
    ROUND(AVG(process_time)::numeric, 3) as processing_time
FROM (
    SELECT
        s.machine_id,
        s.process_id,
        (e.timestamp - s.timestamp) as process_time
    FROM
        Activity as s, Activity as e
    WHERE
        s.activity_type = 'start' and
        e.activity_type = 'end' and
        s.process_id = e.process_id and
        s.machine_id = e.machine_id
)
GROUP BY machine_id

    VALUES
        ('Low Salary'),
        ('Average Salary'),
        ('High Salary')
) as c(category) LEFT JOIN (
    select
        case
            when income < 20000 then 'Low Salary'
            when income between 20000 and 50000 then 'Average Salary'
            else 'High Salary'
        end as category,
        count(*) as accounts_count
    from Accounts group by category
) as a ON c.category=a.category

FROM
(
    (
        SELECT

        FROM RequestAccepted ra
        GROUP BY requester_id
    )

    (
        SELECT

    )
